method.step1_load_clean: Unemployment CSV read with encoding='utf-8-sig'; kept [State/Area, Year, Month, 'Percent (%) of Labor Force Unemployed in State/Area']; dropped non-state rows ('Los Angeles County','New York city'); mapped 51 state names (50 states + 'District of Columbia'->DC) to 2-letter USPS (0 unmapped); rate parsed via strip + comma removal + to_numeric; month_start = to_datetime(year, month, day=1). ZHVI CSV read wide (51 states x 291 month-END columns 1996-01..2020-03), dropped 'Unnamed: 0', melted to (state=StateName already USPS, month_start, ZHVI), date labels normalized to month start via to_period('M').to_timestamp(), NaN ZHVI dropped, (state, month_start) de-duplicated by mean (0 duplicates found).
method.step2_zhvi_rolling: Per state: reindex ZHVI onto gap-free month-start range 1996-01..2020-03 (needed so 2010-01 has a populated window), then rolling(12, min_periods=6).mean() and .std() -> ZHVI_Rolling_Mean / ZHVI_Rolling_Std (computed on full history, then subset to window).
method.step3_unemployment_rolling: Same treatment on the 1976-01..2025-11 history -> Unemployment_Rolling_Mean / Unemployment_Rolling_Std (rolling 12, min_periods=6).
method.step4_cross_correlation: Per state both rolling-mean series reindexed to the complete monthly index pd.date_range('2010-01-01','2019-12-01', freq='MS') (120 months), missing filled with .ffill().bfill(). For each lag k in -24..+24: r(k) = Pearson corr(ZHVI_Rolling_Mean[t], Unemployment_Rolling_Mean[t+k]) computed as corr(a, b.shift(-k)) over overlapping dropna pairs (>=96 obs per lag; correlation is mean/variance-normalized by construction). Sign convention: k<0 -> 'Unemployment leads ZHVI', k>0 -> 'ZHVI leads Unemployment', k==0 -> 'Synchronous'.
method.step5_ranking: Per state lag_star = argmax|r(k)| (deterministic tie-break: smaller |lag|, then smaller lag), correlation, abs_correlation (4 dp), relationship label; states ranked by abs_correlation desc; significant = abs_correlation > 0.1 (strict); top 10 exported.

caveats: All 51 states exceed the |r| > 0.1 threshold; correlations are extremely high and negative because both series are 12-month smoothed and strongly trend over 2010-2019 (ZHVI rising, unemployment falling from its post-2009 peak).

The lag profile is nearly monotone in |lag| for most states, so 37 of 51 states hit the -24 boundary. The boundary argmax indicates the specified method cannot reliably pin down a lead time at the edge of the +/-24 search window; interior optima are more interpretable (e.g. CA -14, HI -16, AZ -17, DC -7, NV -13).
Correlations are level correlations of smoothed non-stationary series, not pre-whitened; they measure co-movement and are not evidence of causal lead-lag.
